items.question: explain the difference between fusion on and fusion off
items.text: Fusion on refers to the state where a computer's CPU utilizes both its core and hyper-threading technologies to execute tasks, thereby increasing processing power and efficiency. Conversely, fusion off denotes the state where the CPU operates with reduced capabilities, possibly disabling hyper-threading or other advanced features to save energy or meet specific performance requirements.
